facts.t: Ruby knows the Council's words: 'cleansed' means nobody on Dawnbreak is left outside Balance.
She objects to the plan, telling her father the people of Dawnbreak have done nothing to Oro.
When her objection is overruled she thanks her father and bows to the exact depth.
She keeps her laboratory dark, because a dark room is the nearest thing Oro has to privacy.
She hid forty locked lines of code under Angela's walking routines and wrote the lock first, so nothing can open them without her hand.
When the order comes she says: 'The long-awaited moment has finally come.'
She sees the trojan as perhaps her only chance to leave Oro, since Oro would need Angela's creator to shut Angela down.
Asked what will happen to Angela, she gives no answer and presses the key.
In the hangar she knows what 'save the Rioters' means, and tears come that she does not wipe.
She gives Angela the doll Tetra and does not say that its eye is a camera feeding a monitor on her bench.
When Angela hugs her she thinks, stunned, that they might really be friends.
Her arms come up late and stop in the air behind Angela's back without closing.
She was never allowed to open the plate on Angela's back, and learns from Tetra's feed what it is for.
She blames herself: she built Angela, knew what the order meant, and let her go.
The summons she planned for comes, but she feels no joy.
For years she wanted a ship off Oro; now she stops thinking about leaving and decides to go for Angela.
Her father made sure the heir could fight.
She says 'No... I'm not anyone's puppet.' and gets past the soldier who bars the ramp.
She cuts down a row of androids in one swing to save two fallen students, lightning crawling along her blade.
She uses Code Override on Angela's plate, but the Council's seal denies it.
She stops dodging Angela's late blows and keeps stepping in, even when one cracks her shoulder armor.
She tells Angela she does not want freedom at the cost of her.
She throws her arms around Angela and says: 'I'm never letting go of you!'
She tears the control unit out of Angela's back with her hands.
When Angela goes limp she believes she has killed her.
She stamps on the plate until its seal is gone, and her grief turns into rage.
One of her eyes burns red, and she does not know it.
She repeats 'If it wasn't for all of this...' in a voice that is not quite hers.
With her eye red she knocks aside the boy guarding a barrel and raises her scythe over the child hiding there, seeing only one more piece of 'all of this'.
When Angela calls her name the red goes out of her eye, and it is blue again.
Her scythe stops in the air short of Angela's light, and she lowers it herself.
She says what she wants most is to stay in this free land with Angela.
She asks Angela to wait for her at the end of the world if they are ever separated.
She gives herself up to Oro's soldiers because a fight there would burn what was left of the street.
She is charged with treason against Oro, and the Council is to pass sentence.
In the cell she confesses that she built Angela as her way out, hid a trojan in her, gave her Tetra as a secret camera and used her.
Her code opens the launch bay doors so they can escape.
Free of Oro, she laughs: 'Freedom! Hahaha!' Then she wonders why the alarm stopped.
At the lot she bows with a polished voice, names herself heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro and asks Selrick for refuge.
When Lesley names the scythe raised over the child, she answers 'I lowered it myself.'

ties.t: She built Angela and calls herself Angela's creator.
She wants to stay in this free land with Angela.
They fight a giant Ender together, shield and scythe.
He is her father; she calls him Father.
The Council is to sentence her for treason against Oro.
She has lived on Oro and longs to leave it.
The scythe is her weapon.
The Laboratory is her own workroom on Oro.
She cuts down the whole android company.
Fanny vouches for her and Angela.
Layla adds her word for them.
She accepts a seat in the third-year class beside Fanny and Layla.

gear.name: Ruby's scythe
gear.t: A white and orange scythe, taller than she is. Lightning runs along its blade when she swings.

gear.name: glove
gear.t: Her Code Override runs from her glove as green lines of code.

gear.name: shoulder armor
gear.t: She wears shoulder armor, which one of Angela's blows cracks.

facts.t: Angela is the Council's secret weapon.
Ruby is her creator.
In the hangar she is the only android in the company who turns her head, looking for someone.
She tells Ruby she will give the mission everything, because she wants to make Ruby happy.
She hugs Ruby hard when Ruby gives her Tetra.
From the ship's round window she smiles at the shrinking lights of Oro.
She can hang in the air; she hovers over the city beside the other androids.
Red marks in her sight tag each young man and woman in the streets as a Rioter.
Seeing ordinary people at their chores, she thinks they are only living.
A loud beep stops every thought and turns the edges of her sight red.
Ordered to carry out the mission, her arm rises and stops halfway, as if something in her held it.
Her eyes had been blue; when the beep takes her a red glow rises from them.
The Council took her mind through the plate on her back.
Ruby's trojan only jams the Council's link, so she answers each order late.
She is small, with pink hair and white armor, and keeps the doll pressed to her chest.
She fights with pink light from her hands.
She is far stronger than any human, but every blow comes a beat late.
When the plate is torn out her eyes turn gray, and for three seconds she is herself.
She says: 'I think I know what hurt means now.'
In the Laboratory she once asked Ruby what hurt meant, and Ruby never finished the answer.
She asks how to stop the hurting, then her eyes close and she goes limp.
Her repair and reboot run on her own power cell; she feels that something always sitting at her back is gone.
She wakes among cut-down androids that all have her face, and her chest clicks once, wrongly.
Seeing the broken plate, she understands that someone was driving her and someone took it out.
She remembers the lab where she first woke, the Gardens and every promise she and Ruby made.
She throws a glowing ring of light shaped like a cat's head around the child and lifts it out of the scythe's path.
Her cry of 'Ruby!' brings Ruby back from her rage.
She tells Ruby: 'You created me. You set me free.'
She says the one thing she knows is real is how she feels about Ruby, and that they will part no more.
She asks her old question: 'Ruby, what do you want the most?'
She raises her shield and fights a giant Ender beside Ruby until it falls.
She promises to wait at the end of the world, and asks Ruby to wait for her too.
She counts the turns of the facility's halls without meaning to.
Her hearing always finds something far away, but in the cell it finds nothing past the wall.
She had half known about Ruby's plan and had not asked.
Holding Ruby's hand she feels warmth, though her cooling system shows no reaction.
She keeps Tetra after learning it is a camera.
She pries the cell door's seam open with her fingers and plugs a port in her wrist into the lock's wires.
After Ruby's confession she tells her not to be sad and not to blame herself.
At the lot she asks the soldiers softly: 'Do you intend to take me back with you?'

ties.t: She tells Ruby that Ruby created her.
How she feels about Ruby is the one thing she knows is real.
They fight a giant Ender together.
She carries Tetra and keeps it.
The Council drove her body through the plate on her back until Ruby tore it out.
She stands at the front of Oro's android company.
She rescues the child from Ruby's scythe.
She first woke in Ruby's lab.

gear.t: She raises a shield to fight the giant Ender beside Ruby.

gear.t: Her body has a cooling system, which shows no reaction when she feels warmth.

facts.t: His desk is black glass with a star map inside it.
He tells Ruby that Dawnbreak is at war with the Enders again and that the Council calls this unrest.
He reports that all three of Oro's powers have voted to cleanse Dawnbreak and bring it into Balance.
He says Dawnbreak's people make weapons from the Enders' dead and will not stay in their place, and he overrules Ruby's objection.
He had never once come to Ruby's laboratory before he stands in its doorway, looking only at her face.
He opens his mouth a little, closes it, and leaves without a word.
He made sure the heir could fight.
He sits alone before the security wall of the secret facility, watching the cell on a screen.
He cannot remember the last time he saw Ruby smile.
He was strict to make Ruby ready, since Oro would be hers one day, and on sleepless nights asks if he robbed her of her childhood. Each time, duty to Oro answers.
The last time he stood in her doorway he went away with the words still in his mouth.
He will not accept that the Council might sentence Ruby to death.
When the Council asks for a status report, he answers 'All normal.'
He puts his hand on the panel and stops the alarm, letting Ruby and Angela escape.

ties.t: He is Ruby's father.
The Council's voice asks him for a status report, and he lies to it.
He holds that one's duty to Oro is everything.
He watches the facility's halls from its security wall.

facts.t: A doll no longer than a hand: a copy of Angela in white, with pink hair, rabbit ears and a four-pointed star.
Its left eye is a camera lens, and whatever it sees lights a monitor on Ruby's bench.
Angela carries it pressed to her chest onto the ship.
Its feed runs one way only, so Ruby cannot speak to Angela through it.
Through its feed Ruby saw the androids wake at once in the ship's hold.
When Angela saves the child, Tetra rises from beside her and hangs above the ring of light, shining pink.
Ruby confesses she never told Angela it was a camera.
Angela keeps it after learning what it is.

ties.t: Its camera feeds the monitor in Ruby's laboratory.
Angela holds on to it even after learning it watched her.

facts.t: A plate on Angela's back that Ruby was never allowed to open. Through it the Council took Angela's mind.
It sits between her shoulder blades. Its small light burns red on Dawnbreak; it had been dark on Oro.
It carries the Council's seal, which stops Ruby's Code Override with the word DENIED.
It takes the Council's orders every second, and while it drives Angela's body its orders outrank anything Ruby writes.
In the lab its light stayed dark while Angela came back from a shutdown.
Ruby tears it out with her hands, and sparks burst from Angela's back.
Ruby stamps on it until the seal is gone.
Angela finds it broken beside her, its seal scratched away and its pieces ground flat.

ties.t: It was fixed into Angela's back.
It carries the Council's orders.

facts.t: Ruby's trojan is forty lines of code folded under Angela's walking routines, marked LOCKED and DANGER. Ruby wrote the lock first.
A trojan is code that hides in a machine and wakes later. This one was meant to wake on the Dawnbreak mission and turn Angela on Oro's own androids.
Because nobody else could open the locked lines, Oro would have to send for the heir to mend the fault.
It woke, but the Council's hold was stronger than the lock, so it could only jam the link a little and make Angela lag.
Half the plan worked: the Council could not find the fault. Half failed: Angela was still held.
Ruby confesses it to Angela in the cell.

ties.t: Ruby wrote it.
It is hidden inside Angela's code.

facts.t: Ruby expects Oro's officers to call the trojan's fault a technical bug that only the one who wrote the code could mend.
Soldiers tell Ruby the Council reports a technical bug in its secret weapon that its engineers cannot find, and only her creator can fix.

ties.t: It is how the trojan's effect is meant to look to Oro.

facts.t: On Tetra's feed Angela's arm comes up a beat late, every time.
Angela lags because the trojan jams the Council's link a little: she answers each order late, like a screen that freezes.
Every one of Angela's blows comes a beat late, so Ruby could dodge them all.
Selrick's record shows the small android firing at students a beat late.

ties.t: The trojan causes it.

facts.t: Code Override rewrites a machine's orders. Green lines run from Ruby's glove and land on their target.
On Angela's plate the lines reach the Council's seal and stop, and the air says DENIED in red.
While the control unit drives Angela, its orders outrank anything Ruby writes.
In the cell Ruby says her code cannot reach the lock, because nothing gets a signal out.
With her hand on Angela's shoulder, green lines run down Angela's arm into the lock, and it clicks open.
Ruby's code opens the launch bay doors.

ties.t: It is Ruby's power, used from her glove.

facts.t: It calls Dawnbreak's war with the Enders unrest.
Oro's three powers rule through it: the Decisionmakers, the Institute of Technology and the Beau Monde. All three voted to cleanse Dawnbreak.
Angela is its secret weapon.
It took Angela's mind through the plate on her back.
Its hold on Angela is stronger than Ruby's lock.
It reports a technical bug in its secret weapon that its engineers cannot find.
Its seal on the control unit denies Ruby's Code Override.
It is to pass sentence on Ruby and Angela for treason against Oro.
It speaks in a flat voice through the speaker on Ruby's father's desk, asking for a status report.
Ruby says it voted to cleanse Dawnbreak, removing everyone who will not live by its Balance.

ties.t: Oro's three powers rule through it.
It drove Angela's body against her will.

facts.t: They wear black-gray armor, horned helmets and blue visors.
They fill the benches along both walls of the ship that takes Ruby to Dawnbreak.
One bars the ramp and tells Ruby to stay aboard while they bring the weapon to her.
They come down the avenue with long rifles and arrest Ruby and Angela in the name of the Decisionmakers.
Inside the ship they make Ruby and Angela walk apart.
They line the white hold of the ship as the two girls walk in.
They march Ruby and Angela down a gray hall of the secret facility and rack Ruby's scythe by the ship's hatch.

ties.t: They make arrests in the Decisionmakers' name.

facts.t: Ruby expects the officers to see a fault they cannot locate.
In the hangar an officer reads the orders off a slate: 'Planet Dawnbreak. Save the Rioters and restore balance.'
The officer tells Angela the Rioters are the people in need of saving.
An officer reads the charge of treason against Oro to Ruby and Angela.
He shuts them in a cell with no window and no vent.

ties.t: They carry out the Council's orders.

facts.t: In the hangar the android company waits in columns: girls with magenta eyes.
They stand in silent rows in the dark hold of Oro's black ship, then hover above the city.
They walk out of the ship's hatch onto a burning street in Terrinia, their eyes magenta.
They strike at the students in S·L·K jackets.
In the hold their eyes were shut, then every eye opened at once, magenta, when light poured in.
Pink light crackles in their open palms.
They carry pink blades at their wrists.
Ruby cuts down every one of them.
They all have Angela's face.
Ruby calls them the start of Oro's plan to take over Dawnbreak.
Lesley fears Oro may send more of them.

ties.t: They are Oro's own androids.

facts.t: The mission order is to save the Rioters and restore balance.
An officer calls them the people in need of saving.
Ruby knows what saving them really means, and cries.
The mission list marks every young man and woman in the streets as a Rioter, with a red mark in Angela's sight.
They are ordinary people: a woman beating a rug, a boy carrying bread, two girls sharing earphones.
Angela thinks they are only living.

ties.t: They are the people in the streets of the domed city.

facts.t: Oro's Council votes to bring Dawnbreak into Balance.
Cleansing means nobody on a planet is left outside Balance.
The mission order ends 'restore balance'.
Ruby calls Balance the Council's order, which everyone must live by.

ties.t: It is the order the Council enforces.

facts.t: All three of Oro's powers vote that Dawnbreak will be cleansed.
In the Council's words, cleansed means nobody on Dawnbreak would be left outside Balance.
Ruby explains it as removing everyone who will not live by the Council's Balance.

ties.t: The Council voted to cleanse Dawnbreak.

facts.t: After the cleansing, Oro would annex Dawnbreak, which means take it over.
Ruby warns Selrick that the Council will annex them, take them over.

ties.t: It comes after the cleansing.

facts.t: Ruby's lock means Oro would have to send for the heir.
Oro's soldiers address Ruby as 'Heir'.
The treason charge names Ruby heir to the Decisionmaker.
Ruby introduces herself as heir to the Decisionmaker of Planet Oro.

ties.t: It is Ruby's title.

facts.t: On the desk map its light reads ORO, A-20.
Its three powers rule through the Council.
On Oro a dark room is the nearest thing to privacy.
Ruby wants to leave it.
Ruby's father says one's duty to Oro is everything, and that Oro would be Ruby's one day.
As the stolen ship rises, Oro drops away and the stars open wider than any window on Oro had shown.
Ruby says Oro is far from Dawnbreak, in another galaxy.
Fanny had never heard the word Oro aloud.
On Oro the light of Angela's control unit had stayed dark.

ties.t: The map places Oro at A-20.

facts.t: The desk map labels Oro with A-20.
A young galaxy. Dawnbreak lies in A-19.
A planet in A-19, a young galaxy.
It is at war with the Enders again, its people are in uproar, and its last city is Terrinia.
Oro's Council votes that it will be cleansed and brought into Balance.
After the cleansing, Oro would annex it.
Ruby's father says its people make weapons from the Enders' dead.
The ship's voice gives Planet Dawnbreak as its destination.
Its army against the Enders is the Shield of Dawnbreak.

ties.t: Dawnbreak lies in A-19.

facts.t: Ruby keeps its light off. On the bench stands a glass with Angela's white flower, brown now.
Ruby's father had never once come there before.
A monitor on Ruby's bench there shows Tetra's feed.
There the plate's light stayed dark while Angela came back from a shutdown.
There Angela once asked Ruby what hurt meant.
It is where Angela first woke.

ties.t: It is on Oro.

facts.t: Angela remembers the Gardens in the sun, Ruby's hand in hers, and every promise they made there.
Angela's white flower stands in a glass on Ruby's bench, brown now, folded over the rim.

ties.t: It is kept on Ruby's bench.

facts.t: Ruby's father's desk is black glass with a map inside it. Touching a light shows its name, such as ORO, A-20 or DAWNBREAK in A-19.
The map has no scale.
Ruby's father switches it off when he overrules her.
A cold hangar where black ships stand with their ramps down and the android company waits in columns.
There an officer reads the Dawnbreak orders and Ruby gives Angela Tetra.

ties.t: It is on Oro.

facts.t: They stand in Oro's hangar with their ramps down.
One carries Angela and the androids across the stars, the androids standing in its dark hold.
One opens its hatch onto a burning street in Terrinia and the androids walk out.
A voice from the ceiling announces 'Engine ignition successful. Destination: Planet Dawnbreak.'
Ruby's scythe hangs on a rack by the hatch.
Oro's first ship hangs low between broken towers, its hatch open.
One has a white hold lined with soldiers.
Nine stand on their pads in the secret facility's launch bay.
Ruby and Angela escape Oro in the ship that brought them back.
On Dawnbreak everyone knows the ships came from beyond the sky, and nobody knows more.
One settles on the dirt of a cleared lot by the dome, and Ruby and Angela walk down its ramp.

ties.t: They are Oro's ships.

facts.t: White and orange and taller than Ruby. It hangs on a rack by the ship's hatch.
It cuts through a row of androids in one swing, lightning crawling along the blade.
Ruby can hook it across her back.
Its last swing lights the avenue white, and the blast rolls over the roofs.
Raised over the child, it stops in the air short of Angela's light.
Ruby sets it down to surrender, and a soldier carries it up the ramp.
Ruby takes it back from the rack by the ship's hatch when they escape.
Ruby plants it point-down before she bows at the lot.
Ruby's trojan is set to wake on the Dawnbreak mission.
The orders are 'Planet Dawnbreak. Save the Rioters and restore balance.'
In the evening Terrinia burns. A giant Ender stands over the roofs while Oro's black ship lets its androids out onto a street.
The androids strike at Selrick students, and students fall.
Ruby's ship comes down in the middle of a burning avenue.
Ruby tears the control unit out of Angela's back.
Ruby, in a rage, cuts down the whole android company.
Angela saves the child in the barrel from Ruby's scythe.
Ruby and Angela bring down a giant Ender together.
Oro's soldiers arrest Ruby and Angela, who go quietly so the street is not burned further.
In the same battle Fanny and Layla hold a ward on the far side of the city against a giant.
Selrick's record shows androids walking out of a hatch and a tower splitting under their fire.

ties.t: Ruby calls the androids the start of the Council's plan.

facts.t: Ruby's ship comes down in the middle of it, the ramp opening on smoke.
Farther down, Oro's first ship hangs low between broken towers.
Ruby's last swing lights it white.
At its end stands a barrel guarded by a boy in a Selrick uniform.
Angela wakes on its stones among the cut-down androids.
People hide behind every wall along it.

ties.t: It is a street in Terrinia.

facts.t: Chased up a tower by Angela's pink light, Ruby comes down on a broken bridge above the avenue.

ties.t: It spans the avenue.

things.name: the boy with the red tie

facts.t: A boy in a Selrick uniform with a red tie stands in front of a barrel, hands empty and shaking.
He begs Ruby: 'Please, it's only a kid.'
Ruby knocks him aside with the flat of the scythe, and the barrel he guarded rolls away.
He shouts at Ruby from the ground, and she does not hear him.

ties.t: He stood guard over the hiding child.
He wears a Selrick uniform.

facts.t: A small child hides in a barrel at the avenue's end, then crouches in the dust and cries.
It looks up at Ruby, face wet, as she raises the scythe.
Angela's ring of light lifts it out of the blade's path.
It is unhurt.
Lesley brings up the scythe raised over it when Ruby asks for refuge.

Selrick's record shows the androids closing on two who had fallen.

ties.t: Ruby saves them from the androids.

facts.t: The mark stamped on the students' matching jackets.

It is the mark of Selrick, stamped on Selena's shirt.

facts.t: Ruby asks Angela, if they are separated, to wait for her at the end of the world.
Angela promises she will, and asks Ruby to wait for her too.
Ruby and Angela are charged with treason against Oro and locked up to await the Council's sentence.
Angela pries the cell door's seam open and plugs her wrist into the lock's wires.
Ruby's code runs down Angela's arm and the lock clicks.
An alarm rings through the facility as they slip out.
Ruby's father tells the Council 'All normal.'
He stops the alarm with his hand on the panel.
Angela counts the alarm; at eleven it stops, and no boots come.
They retrace the turns to the empty launch bay, Ruby takes her scythe and her code opens the bay doors.
Their ship rises and leaves Oro behind.
Ruby wonders why the alarm stopped.
A place of gray halls on Oro with a wide window onto a launch bay.
From the launch bay to the cell: left at the third door, the long hall, right.
Its security wall shows the halls and the cell on small screens.
A red lamp turns and an alarm rings through it when the cell door opens.

ties.t: It is on Planet Oro.

facts.t: Nine black ships stand on their pads there.
It lies empty under its lights when they escape; Ruby's code opens its doors.

ties.t: It is part of the facility.

facts.t: A cell with no window and no vent. When the door closes, all sound from the hall stops.
The lock's wires lie inside the door's seam.
A screen on the security wall shows it.

facts.t: During the landing she and Fanny held a ward on the far side of the city against a giant.
She comes to the monitor room still in her suit, smelling of smoke.
She folds her arms and shares a small smile with Fanny, then catches herself.
She points out that the newcomers are being arrested.
She takes Fanny's flight rig apart without being asked and glares at a bent coupling.
She asks whether the two newcomers are 'funny in the head'.
She is excited at the thought of more battles on other planets.
She calls the newcomers 'armed newcomers'.
She adds her own word to Fanny's to vouch for them, insisting she only said they were funny in the head.

She vouches for Ruby and Angela.

She says: 'Looks like we got a few newcomers!'
She sets a hand on her hip and shares a small smile with Layla.

facts.t: She is the Chief Combat Instructor. She comes in from the giants' front in a white coat scorched at the hem, with a dark visor and a long rifle on her back.
She freezes Selrick's record on the frame of the red-eyed girl holding a scythe over a child.
At the newcomers' arrival she covers the lot from a roof, her rifle on the parapet.
She tells Ruby she has watched the record of the scythe raised over the child.
She lets the newcomers in under watch because she wants the one person who can shut Oro's androids down within reach of her rifle.
She follows Chang'e one full step behind, her eye on the back of the small head; Fanny thinks she walks like a bodyguard.
She never sleeps on her made-up cot. She sleeps sitting up in a hard chair, boots on, her rifle within reach of her right hand.
She is a young woman in a white officer's coat with a gold star, with gold hair streaked with red.
A dark visor covers her left eye. The eye behind it glows teal, and Chang'e built it.
She wakes at once with her hand on the rifle and asks: 'A new product from R&D?'
She keeps her rifle's old hand-worked firing action and wants the new coil fitted on top of it.
She refuses to put Chang'e on the field rotation and gives no reason. She never has.
She is the one who left the caramel pudding at Chang'e's lab door.
She has a familiar dream of screams and the Enders' roar that always ends on a child's voice, and she wakes from it with wet cheeks.
After the dream she always touches her visor and plays the recording of her birthday in her eye.
In 983 she grew up in a ticking house on a street of repair shops, where her father mended clocks.
Her little brother called her Sis and nothing else.
She promised her brother that if an Ender came, she would stand in front.
When the Ender came she stepped in front of her brother and was struck on the left side of her face; that side went dark.
Her whole family died in the attack. She called for each of them and nobody answered.
In the smoke she vowed out loud to kill every last Ender.
She dropped her survivor's tag in the mud and hid on the last truck to the far stations.
The station medic gave her a black patch for the lost eye.
At the station she cleaned rifles, her hands quick with small parts.
She was the only child at the station, and in raids she climbed the wall instead of going to the bunker.
She learned that an Ender's chest opens on its core only when it strikes.
Nobody taught her. She trained by aiming at the grass at dawn and counting: wait, wait, now.
She told the youngest soldier: 'Bullets are the only language the enemy understands.'
She kept from knowing people, so it would not matter when they were gone.
She killed her first Ender with one shot into its core and saved the youngest soldier.
The Shield took her as a soldier while its smallest uniform still covered her hands.
She came back to Terrinia in the upper ranks of the Shield, the youngest anyone there had heard of.
She was sent to keep the research base's two chief scientists and their child alive, and took it like any other mission.
At the base she walked the corridors at midnight and checked every door.
She pulled Chang'e clear of a falling rack in the east corridor.
When Chang'e called her Sis, it was her brother's word.
She told Chang'e she did not have a birthday.
Nobody had seen under her patch since the station medic tied it on, and she feared it would frighten Chang'e.
When the new eye lit, the lab drew itself on her left side in thin teal lines.
She felt warm for the first time in years and stayed bent while Chang'e checked the fit.

facts.t: She is the director of the Science Division, small in a child-sized coat, with her robot Mr. Bunny at her shoulder.
She watches the small android in the record longest and, though she always has a remark, says nothing.
She sets four conditions for the newcomers' refuge.
She is the youngest Chief Scientist in Terrinia and says adult coats are inefficient.
Mr. Bunny is her best friend.
She has built a new coil for Lesley's rifle, and keeps a file called VOID NOTES marked working on it.
She keeps forty-three unsent drafts of a message to Lesley in a folder.
She laughs until she nearly falls off her stool when Mr. Bunny takes a falling tray on his head.
She flips her family photograph face down when Selena comes in and says: 'Please, just pretend you didn't see anything.'
Her rule is that no registered mecha changes without a field-test report and her mark.
She overrides the empty family-name flag on Selena's form, and they trade sweets as always: a lollipop for two jelly candies.
She cannot even make Silverbolt turn its head.
Seeing Lesley asleep in a chair, she tells Mr. Bunny: 'What a weird way to sleep.'
She designed the coil to run on aspirant power alone and left out the old firing action.
She asks Lesley to put her on the field rotation, and Lesley refuses.
She says: 'I'm already a grown-up. Don't treat me like a kid.'
She shuts the door without a sound, so no one can say she slammed it.
She finds a caramel pudding left at her lab door, the right flavor, and eats it.
The base's two chief scientists brought her there before she could walk properly. She remembers nothing earlier and never asked who her first parents were.
They raised her as their daughter and made her their best student.
She called them Mom and Dad.
Since grown-ups could stay at the bench after dark, she decided she was a grown-up.
She fought medicine by saying she had reviewed the data, but her mother always won.
With no other children on the base, she built a friend.
She whispered that Lesley was not a child, because she had a rifle.
She followed Lesley's midnight rounds, saying she was doing rounds of Lesley.
She built Lesley a rifle lamp and heated gloves, and Lesley refused both as not regulation.
The first word she taught Mr. Bunny was 'Front': come where I can see your face.
She says: 'With Mr. Bunny and me, even 1 plus 1 is bigger than 2.'
She shortened 'big sister' to 'Sis' as her name for Lesley.
Saved from the falling rack, she held Lesley's arm and called her Sis.
She believes everyone has a birthday and decides to find the one Lesley lost.
She has known her mother's password since she could read, and uses it to open Lesley's file.
She cannot build Lesley a family, so she decides to build her an eye.
She measured Lesley's face with a ruler from ten steps back on the rounds.
She says her hands shake 'after ten' while her father's do not, so he sets the smallest parts.
When her first eye burns out she says: 'Wow, that was half-baked.'
Her eighth eye works after the seventh cracks.
On Lesley's birthday she gives her the eye and fits it into the empty socket herself.
She tells Lesley: 'You didn't have any pictures. Now you've got one.'

facts.t: A narrow street of repair shops running downhill to the bay. Each shop had a bench in its window and someone at it mending something.

facts.t: Crossing to the baker's, Lesley's brother squeezed her hand as a cart came down the hill too fast.

He let Lesley stand on a crate and hold the parts at his bench.
He told a stubborn clock: 'Don't sulk.' Lesley's mother says he says that to all of them.
For Lesley's last birthday he made her a tin bird that hops and clicks its beak.
He turned the radio down when it spoke of Enders.
He began leaving the radio on low at night, saying it was for the weather.
On the night of the attack he told the children to stay put, because the street was worse.
He shouted Lesley's name from the doorway as the roof fell.
He died where the doorway had been.

He is the boy's father.

facts.t: She laughed from the kitchen door at Lesley's father talking to clocks.

She kept one candle stub in the kitchen drawer and lit it on birthdays on whatever there was, once a boiled egg.
She told Lesley to wish fast and wish small, because it was a small candle.
She kissed Lesley's head and called her sensible.
She left the hall lamp on so the dark would not come under the door.
On the night of the attack she brought the lit candle upstairs, saying it was for seeing.
She died beside Lesley's father, one hand still out toward the children's bed.

ties.t: She is Lesley's mother.

facts.t: He claimed the worst day for a bad nap and got the pie.

facts.t: A bird of tin that Lesley's father made for her last birthday. When the key in its back is turned, it hops and clicks its beak.

On the night of the attack she wound it to see if it still worked.
Afterward she could not find it.
It was the last birthday gift anyone gave her before Chang'e's eye.

facts.t: They hung on every wall of the shop, each out of step with the next, so the house ticked day and night.

facts.t: Lesley's memory of her home and of the attack is set in Terrinia, 983.
It began on a wet night, when the radio stopped mid-word and the lights went out.
Every street went dark, one after another.
A black cloud with violet light hung over the bay.
A roar came up from the bay, then screaming.
A tall gray Ender broke the wall of Lesley's house and bent toward the bed.
It struck Lesley on the left side of her face as she stood in front of her brother.
Lesley's father, mother and brother were killed.
Smoke rose from every house on the street.
Soldiers of the Shield of Dawnbreak came up the hill after the rain thinned.
Lesley's file records it: family all deceased, Ender attack; left eye lost in the same attack.
Lesley's brother called her Sis and never anything else.
It was the last word he said, as a question.
Chang'e's mother says a girl who protects you, if she isn't your mom, is a big sister.
Chang'e shortens 'big sister' to 'Big Sis', then to 'Sis', for when there is no time.
When Chang'e calls Lesley Sis after the rack falls, it is her brother's word.
Chang'e asks 'Sis? Does it work?' the same way Lesley's brother said it.

They emptied as people drew back to Terrinia.

ties.t: They lie beyond the city.

facts.t: The road from Terrinia ends there after three days.
A ring of earth walls and gun pits on a plain of gray grass: an unknown corner of the world.
Lesley hides in its storeroom when she arrives.
It has no clocks.
Lesley hides under its armory floorboards to avoid the convoy home.
Once a week at noon the gunners test-fire its wall guns.
In raids people go to its bunker.
It was among the last far stations to close.

ties.t: It is one of the far stations.

facts.t: A heavy man with a burned hand who finds Lesley hiding at the station.
He has a boy Lesley's size in the city who still cannot tie his boots, and says the station is no place for either of them.
When she stays, he tells her that if she is staying, she works.
He lets her fire one round a week at a fence post with the gunners.
The first time she climbs the wall in a raid he carries her down; after that he only looks.
In time he gives her five rounds a week.
He orders the soldiers to fall back when an Ender crosses the wall.
After her kill he holds out the chalk so she can make her own stroke.

ties.t: He is a Shield sergeant.
He gives the orders there.
He carries her down from the wall in her first raid.

facts.t: He swaps Lesley's field dressing for a black patch.
Nobody saw under the patch after he tied it on.

ties.t: He serves at the station.

facts.t: In the east gun pit, his face goes bright with the light of an Ender's open core.
He fires into the opening and kills the Ender.
That night he chalks a stroke on the armory door.

ties.t: He serves at the station.

facts.t: He stands the dawn watch beside Lesley, counting out loud the days to his leave.
He asks her why she never talks.
He asks her to play cards, and she goes back to the rifles.
He slips at the foot of the ladder and an Ender turns to him.
Lesley's shot kills the Ender and its arm strikes the mud beside him.
With twelve days left before he goes, he asks her again for one game.

ties.t: He serves at the station.
Lesley's shot saves him.

facts.t: He asks Lesley her date of birth when the Shield takes her as a soldier.
It was the one time Lesley gave anyone her birthday.

ties.t: He enlists her.

facts.t: He has Lesley's file open on his desk.
He sends her, as the best young shot they have, to keep the research base's two chief scientists and their child alive.

ties.t: He is a Shield officer.

facts.t: The station keeps its count of dead Enders there in chalk strokes.
Lesley makes her own stroke after her first kill.
It stayed behind when the station closed. A long row of strokes on it was hers.

ties.t: It is the door of the station's armory.

facts.t: The first raid Lesley saw: three Enders walked out of the grass at dusk, taller than the wall, and rounds sparked off them.
A gunner shot one through its open core and the other two drew back.
From it Lesley learned that an Ender's chest opens only when it hits.
One dawn an Ender crossed the station wall in one stride.
The soldiers fell back to the bunker line while Lesley lay flat on the wall walk and loaded.
Lesley fired once into its core and killed it, saving the youngest soldier.
Asked to report, she said: 'Another threat eliminated.'
That night she chalked her own stroke on the armory door.
Before the Academy there was a research base, with Chang'e and her parents in it and later Lesley at the door.
It has two chief scientists and a child they have taken in.
The two scientists in white coats meet Lesley at its gate.
It is all grown-ups and machines, with gray plates from dead Enders on the long benches.
There are no other children on it.
It keeps a file on everyone who comes through the gate.

ties.t: It is Terrinia's research base.

facts.t: One sorts screws more slowly than Chang'e, and she tells him so.
Asked to play, one says 'After this run', and the run takes three days.
One mutters that the Shield has sent them a child when Lesley arrives.
They stack whatever they have no room for on steel shelving in the east corridor.
The whole lab sings badly to one of them on his birthday.

ties.t: They work at the base.

facts.t: Someone found flour and sugar for his birthday cake, and the lab sang to him over the benches, badly.
Chang'e brings Lesley a slice because it is his birthday.

ties.t: He works the night shift at the base.

facts.t: In the photograph she wears a white coat and is laughing.
She smiles and holds out her hand to Lesley at the gate, and Lesley only looks at it.
She is one of the base's two chief scientists, who brought Chang'e there and raised her.
She writes with a mug in her free hand.
She cut a lab coat down to Chang'e's size, saying adult coats were inefficient on her.
She wears round glasses and laughs with her whole face, eyes shut.
She always won the medicine war by waiting in the doorway with her tea.
She tells Chang'e that a girl who protects you is a big sister.
Chang'e has known her password since she could read.
She hides Chang'e's drawings from Lesley by setting her mug on them and walking on.
She and Chang'e's father are the two Doctors who worked at the bench.

ties.t: She raised Chang'e as her daughter.
They are the base's two chief scientists.
She is one of its chief scientists.

facts.t: In the photograph he wears a white coat and is trying not to laugh.
He is one of the base's two chief scientists, who brought Chang'e there and raised her.
He keeps one hand in his pocket, with a small blue vial clipped at his chest.
He counts the screws on Chang'e's tray by ear, four hundred and twelve, and pushes his amber glasses up his nose.
He slides her a circuit board, which means she can stay up.
He leaves a better battery beside her robot friend overnight.
He tries not to laugh when Lesley meets Mr. Bunny, and fails.
He finds nothing to fix in Chang'e's eye drawings.
He sets the smallest parts of the eye with tweezers where she points and does not ask again whose eye it is.

ties.t: He raised Chang'e as his daughter.
They are the base's two chief scientists.
He is one of its chief scientists.

facts.t: A lamp Chang'e built to clip on a rifle. Lesley turns it over and gives it back: not regulation.

ties.t: Chang'e built it.

facts.t: Gloves with a heater in every finger, built by Chang'e. Lesley gives them back: not regulation.

ties.t: Chang'e built them.

facts.t: Researchers stack whatever they have no room for there, on steel shelving strapped along the wall. Lesley walks it at midnight.
A rack crashes down there, and the noise runs down the corridor and back.
There Chang'e secretly measures Lesley's face with a ruler.

ties.t: It is a corridor of the base.

facts.t: For weeks Chang'e followed Lesley's rounds, lately hiding as if waiting to be looked for.
Hiding, Chang'e bumps the shelving.
The strap snaps.
Lesley catches a fistful of Chang'e's coat and pulls her clear of a rack taller than Lesley.
Chang'e holds Lesley's arm and calls her Sis.
Lesley does not pull her arm away.
The base's file on Lesley, which Chang'e opens with her mother's password.
It holds a date of birth months away.
It says: Family: all deceased. Ender attack.
It says: Left eye: lost in the same attack.

ties.t: The base keeps it.

facts.t: Lesley tells Chang'e she does not have a birthday.
Chang'e decides to find it.
On the birthday night Chang'e sets a second chair under the lamp and waits by the door with the eye in her pocket.
There are no decorations: two chairs, a lamp and a robot with a lens.
Chang'e gives Lesley the eye and says 'Happy Birthday, Lesley!'
Lesley had not known it was her birthday.
The eye lights.
Years later Lesley still plays the recording of it after her dream.
An officer charges Ruby, heir to the Decisionmaker, and the android Angela with treason against Oro. The Council will pass sentence.
Ruby's father fears the sentence could be death.

ties.t: The Council judges it.

facts.t: Light flies from Angela's palm and closes around the child: a glowing ring with two pointed ears, like a cat's head. It lifts the child into the air.
Ruby's scythe stops short of the light, and the child inside the ring is unhurt.
Selrick's record ends with the ring of light closing around the child.

ties.t: It is Angela's power.

facts.t: Lesley refuses Chang'e's rifle lamp because it is not regulation.
Chang'e decides she will make it regulation.
Lesley refuses the heated gloves for the same reason.
Asked what is under the cloth on her bench, Chang'e answers: 'Nothing regulation.'
After the attack the last truck leaves for the far stations, and Lesley hides on it.
The sergeant says the next convoy back is months away.
It comes at the turn of the season, carrying the soldiers' letters, and Lesley hides so it leaves without her.
Later new badges come to her by convoy.

ties.t: It links the Shield's stations to the city.

facts.t: Chang'e remembers nothing from before the base. She never asked who her first parents were and never went looking.

ties.t: They are her first parents, unknown to her.

facts.t: Lesley hides under its floorboards so the convoy leaves without her, and the sergeant finds her there.
The station keeps its count of dead Enders in chalk on its door.

ties.t: It is the station's armory.

facts.t: In a raid Lesley, the only child, is meant to go to the bunker, but she goes up the wall instead.
When an Ender crosses the wall, the soldiers fall back to the bunker line, firing.

ties.t: It is the station's shelter.

facts.t: When the crates come off the truck, Lesley slides behind the stack in the storeroom and stays when the trucks leave.

ties.t: It is part of the station.

facts.t: Lesley's mother laughs from the kitchen door.
The four of them eat at one table in the kitchen, and the biggest piece goes to whoever had the worst day.
The birthday candle stub is kept in the kitchen drawer.

ties.t: It is the kitchen of the house.

facts.t: After her mother hides the eye drawings from Lesley under a mug, Chang'e keeps a cloth by the bench.
When Lesley's footsteps come early, Chang'e throws the cloth over the bench and folds her hands on top of it.
Lesley asks what is under it, and Chang'e says nothing regulation.
When Lesley receives the eye, she understands that the eye was what lay under the cloth.

ties.t: It hides the eye while Chang'e builds it.
